exact_literal_edits.source_excerpt: **M1. Measure-optimality and projections.** With convex R, prove the first variation and necessary/sufficient cone optimality `F'(μ)≥0` everywhere and `F'(μ)=0` μ-a.e. for minimization over nonnegative finite measures, including perturbation integrability. Define h2 by integrating |u|² on angular fibers and h1 by signed w-weight on θ. Distinguish a signed projected measure from a nonnegative lifted representative; never silently treat h1 as positive. Prove the energy/feature-factorization identities and their exact convergence topology, including moment control where needed.

For unfavorable negative-w support use the C.18 trajectory reparametrization: while w≤0 and q=|θ−θ0| is small, w'≥η/2 and q'≤−w(ε+Lq); hence crossing time is at most 2M/η, and ε chosen proportional to r0/(exp(LM²/η)−1) controls q. The printed bound 2/η without M is not a uniform bound for arbitrary w0∈[−M,0]. Prove actual hitting at some time ≤T, not the generally false assertion w(T)=0 for one common fixed T for all w0.

Signed narrow convergence gives norm moments; radial S'=−2(<f,m>+P) gives S=O(t). Failure of either Jordan-part stationarity forces action at least c/(1+t), contradicting finite total dissipation. The full global semiconvexity of |w|W makes W convex by positive-w slices; boundedness and the applicable boundary premise then make W constant. This is a derived consequence of the full hypotheses, not a new constant-penalty assumption. Prove the reflected sign dynamics, robust negative-level trapping, and positive-action escape in both domain branches. At infinity normalize by k=r², prove the compactified fields are uniformly close using the all-f C1 assumption and uniform boundedness, and prove Lyapunov decay through closed boundary-contact time sets before an Arzelà–Ascoli perturbation argument. Do not infer AC from continuity of the compactified energy. The scalar C.18 inequalities still give individual hitting by 2M/η and their proved displacement estimate; the printed 2/η and a common exact hitting time for every w0∈[−M,0] are not valid. Source Assumptions3.4 alone do not imply the advertised global semiconvexity; record the smooth Neumann counterexample honestly, while retaining the full approved library assumptions.
